title: Oval table centre doily
excerpt: An oval doily in lace weight yarn started from a foundation chain to create the elongated shape. Chain arcs and treble fans fill each round to the edge.
sourceNotes: An oval doily worked outward from a short chain foundation, adding rounds of chain arcs and treble groups to reach a table-centre size.

glossaryTerms.definition: An oval shape started from a chain length rather than a ring. Stitches are worked along both sides of the chain to create the elongated base.
The rounded short ends of an oval doily where extra trebles are added to the foundation chain tips to turn the work without drawing in.

crochet.gaugeText: Outer rounds approx. 35 cm x 22 cm.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 35 cm long x 22 cm wide blocked.

content.text: is a chain-20 base. Stitches worked along both sides form the first round, with extra trebles at each

Chain 20. Round 1: work 3 tr into 4th ch from hook, then 1 tr in each of the next 15 chains, then 7 tr into the last chain (curved end). Work back along the other side of the foundation, 1 tr per chain, and 4 tr into the start chain. Join.
Add chain arcs and treble groups every round, increasing at each curved end by working into additional chain spaces. By round 7 the doily should measure approx. 35 cm long.
Fasten off and weave in the end. Block to the oval shape with pins.
